component.name: VPNMan
component.summary: Multi-protocol VPN manager with a kill switch

description.p: VPNMan manages OpenVPN, WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenConnect, Fortinet, SSTP, IKEv2, Tailscale and more from one libadwaita application or an interactive command line, with a built-in network lock (kill switch) for nftables, iptables and pf.

ul.li: Hotspots: the devices behind a Wi-Fi hotspot (GNOME, KDE Plasma, Cinnamon, hostapd) or a shared connection now follow the VPN and the proxies. Start the hotspot first and connect the VPN later, or the other way round: their traffic goes through the tunnel, and with the kill switch on only through it
The proxy (system-wide mode) and the Network Proxy also carry the hotspot's devices (TCP and DNS), and their kill switch blocks them while the proxy is down
Fixed: hotspot devices connected but "no internet" while a VPN was up (TCP segment size too big for the tunnel; the kill switch dropped the hotspot's DHCP requests)
Connections the devices opened before the VPN or the proxy came on are reset so they start again over the right route
New settings connection.share_tunnel (on) and connection.share_ifaces (more interfaces, such as a libvirt bridge)
The packages remove an older script install in /usr/local that would hide the packaged version
Fixed: vpnman doctor stopped with an error after the Proxy engine line
Fixed: the Export menu of the connection table was greyed out (Copy as CSV, Save as CSV)

Network Proxy: send all of this computer's traffic through an HTTP or SOCKS5 proxy, with or without the VPN (after it); Preferences, the Connection page and vpnman netproxy; ignored hosts and programs that skip it
Proxies: Use Fastest, automatic failover to the next favourite, share a proxy as a link or QR code, and "via Cloudflare" shown for servers behind Cloudflare
The connection test checks the proxy; the tray can switch the proxy on and off
Temporary blocks (15 minutes, an hour, a day or until restart); export the connection table as CSV
Disconnecting shows a greyed-out "Disconnecting..." button; the server list shows Connected / Connecting on each server and switches servers from the list
Network Proxy kill switch: if the proxy cannot work, traffic stays blocked instead of going out directly; the connection test checks the proxy, its DNS and IPv6
Reconnects at once when the computer wakes up or the network changes, and per-network rules (connect to a server, turn the network proxy on or off)
Server groups can be reordered and folded; the tray offers the last server and your favourites; Save Diagnostics writes a report with the private parts removed
Password fields turn red when Caps Lock is on
Pop-ups close with Escape and Ctrl+W; the server list loads after a reinstall; the server selector shows full names; Resolve names in the connection table
Check for Updates shows just the new version; install.sh asks whether to install Xray and package.sh builds packages with the same options as GPGMan, with checksums

Proxies through Xray (VLESS, VMess, Trojan, Shadowsocks): a Proxy sub-tab on the Servers page, share links and subscriptions, a local SOCKS5/HTTP proxy or system-wide mode, and proxy only, VPN then proxy, or proxy then VPN
Live table of connections on the Connection page (application, port, protocol, direction), with a pop-out window
Right-click a connection to copy it, force-close it, stop its program or block its address, port or program; a window to manage blocked connections
Edit a whole group or a selection at once: group name, login and SSL tunnel server; multi-select and bulk remove for proxies
Switching servers waits until the old tunnel is completely gone, so WireGuard and OpenVPN never overlap
The server selector on the Connection page shows the server being connected to, or the last connected one
The search box on the Servers page has its own row above the buttons
Windows-only OpenVPN options (register-dns, block-outside-dns, ...) are ignored instead of stopping OpenVPN
Failover lists: choose the servers a profile falls back to, in order (then its group, then favourites)
Importing a config lists the options that will be ignored on this system
Check for Updates in the menu (and optionally once a day)
Servers tab: an "Add Profile" button, for icon themes that lack the header "+" icon
Schedule, app and address bypass, trusted networks, connection test, history and traffic graph, backup and restore, shell completions
A rejected login asks for the credentials and reconnects instead of retrying
Servers tab: select several servers (Ctrl+click, Shift+click, Ctrl+A) and remove them in one go
Switching servers is reliable: no double tunnels, immediate "connecting" feedback, no stale status
OpenVPN configs with Debian-style up/down update-resolv-conf scripts now connect on every distribution
Importing several files reports every failure and no longer creates duplicates on retry
Schedule tab and "vpnman schedule": connect at set times, optionally disconnect again
Apps tab and "vpnman bypass": whitelisted apps skip the VPN and stay online under the kill switch
Fixed the app bypass being bypassed by WireGuard's routing rules
Fixed launching from the app menu when another Python without PyGObject came first in PATH
Installer copies the launcher and icons, restores SELinux contexts, validates the launcher
Removes stale kill-switch and bypass rules at startup and on uninstall; new "vpnman cleanup"
